summary: Lucy reunites with Anda in an online game, where Anda has been promoted to Sergeant. The two miss the high-stakes campaigning they did before, and Lucy reveals she has been discussing factory working conditions with Raymond. Raymond wants factory girls in Ciudad Juarez and Tijuana to strike, but he has struggled to organize them, so Anda offers to join him as a bodyguard inside the game.
one_line: Anda and Lucy return to an online game, miss its old thrills, and join labor organizer Raymond's plan to organize factory girls.
key_facts: Anda was promoted to Sergeant during her absence from the game.
Lucy has been talking to Raymond a lot about the working conditions in the factory.
Anda says she misses the old campaigning, which after the earlier missions makes the game's standard missions seem pale and flat.
Lucy says she thought she was the only one who missed the big fights and big stakes.
The part Anda loved was going up against people who were gaming the game for money rather than playing it.
Raymond says the only way to get results is for workers to band together and withdraw their labour.
Raymond wants the workers to walk out in Ciudad Juarez and Tijuana, not in the game, and plans to call the press in.
Raymond says the problem is getting the girls organized, as he has tried for years in the sewing shops and toy factories.
The bosses lock the doors and keep organizers out, and the girls' parents won't let organizers talk to them.
Raymond hoped the game would let him reach the girls, but he keeps getting killed while trying.
Anda offers to become Raymond's bodyguard and take them to an in-game factory, where the bosses hire mean mercenaries.
Raymond's English is very good, better than Lucy's, though his thick Mexican accent takes some getting used to.
Anda asks Lucy to go get a couple of BFGs, which are weapons in the game.
